title: Rank equal-priority tasks by created_at then id; reject explicit rank for now
context: OA-13: equal-priority actionable tasks were ordered by the opaque priority-then-id tiebreak with no explicit product decision.
decision: Order actionable tasks by priority, then created_at (records missing it sort earliest), then id, in both in-memory and index-backed queries via one shared comparator. Reject an explicit rank field for now: priority already provides the user-control axis, created_at gives equal-priority ties deterministic FIFO semantics, and the schema/migration/surface cost is disproportionate without usage evidence. Do not add a deferred status; todo is the non-actionable backlog after the readiness correction.
consequences: Equal-priority ready work is picked oldest-first across CLI, MCP, dashboard, and the index.
In-memory and index-backed ordering cannot drift because both share byPriorityThenCreatedAtThenId.
No record migration or schema change; explicit rank, if ever justified, becomes a separately phased implementation task.
